title: Stronger Nonprofits Capacity Grants
summary: Grants of $5,000 to $20,000 that help small and mid-sized northern Arizona nonprofits strengthen governance, finances, fundraising, technology, and leadership.
description: Strong communities need strong nonprofits. Stronger Nonprofits Capacity Grants fund time-limited projects that make an organization more effective and resilient, such as a strategic plan, a new financial management system, a fundraising plan, board development, or leadership succession planning.

Capacity grants are paired with the Foundation's Nonprofit Learning Hub. Grantees join a peer cohort that meets four times during the grant year, and many projects use consultants from the Foundation's vetted consultant roster.
Capacity grants do not count against an organization's eligibility for Community Impact Grants.
impact_areas: Fund development planning and donor database systems
Board recruitment, training, and governance policies
Executive transition and leadership succession planning
populations_served: Nonprofit staff, executive directors, and board members
Communities served by small and mid-sized nonprofits

geography.summary: Organizations must be headquartered in Coconino, Yavapai, Navajo, or Apache counties.

eligibility: Tax-exempt under Section 501(c)(3), or a tribal nonprofit program
Headquartered in Coconino, Yavapai, Navajo, or Apache counties
Annual operating budget between $50,000 and $2 million
At least one paid staff member or a full-time volunteer executive
Executive director and board chair commit to participating in the peer learning cohort
not_eligible: Capital equipment unrelated to the capacity project
Organizations that received a Stronger Nonprofits Capacity Grant in 2025 or 2026

how_to_apply.intro: Capacity grants use a two-stage process. Completing the Capacity Readiness Self-Assessment before submitting a letter of inquiry is required.

steps.title: Assess readiness
steps.text: Complete the Capacity Readiness Self-Assessment with your board chair. Attach it to your letter of inquiry.

steps.title: Submit a letter of inquiry
steps.text: Complete the Letter of Inquiry Template and email it with the self-assessment to learning@cinderpeakscf.org by 5:00 p.m. MST on November 13, 2026.

steps.title: Planning conversation
steps.text: Invited applicants meet with the Nonprofit Learning Coordinator to refine the project scope. Invitations are sent by December 4, 2026.

steps.title: Submit the full application
steps.text: Submit the full application, Grant Project Budget Template, and any consultant proposal in the CPCF Grant Portal by 5:00 p.m. MST on January 22, 2027.

steps.title: Decision and cohort launch
steps.text: Awards are announced by February 19, 2027. The first cohort session takes place in March 2027.

review_criteria: The project addresses a clearly identified organizational need
Potential to strengthen the organization's long-term sustainability

reporting.summary: Grantees submit a mid-year progress report and a final grant report, and participate in all four cohort sessions.
items: Changes in organizational practice resulting from the project
reporting.due: Interim report due September 15, 2027; final report due March 31, 2028
